newsitem.title: UK: Stg slumps, dlr revisits levels unseen since 1980s.
newsitem.headline: Stg slumps, dlr revisits levels unseen since 1980s.

text.p: Sterling gave in to profit-takers in European trading on Monday, slumping almost two percent against the mark and probing six-weeks lows against the broadly strong dollar.
The dollar rose to levels not seen since November 1989 - within a whisker of 1.85 marks - as it continued its onslaught on the flagging German currency.

The pound got battered amid a growing perception that a UK interest rate rise might not come as soon as next week when the Bank of England's monetary policy committee meets, dealers said. "Sterling's rally is the product of an environment in which interest rates and being outside EMU are all that matter, and this environment is beginning to shift," said Avinash Persaud, head of currency research at JP Morgan in Europe. "We are beginning to shift into an environment where investors are not only looking at yield." The principal fuel for investors' risk appetite - low interest rates in Germany, Japan and the U.S. - remained in place. "But there is some nervousness over the outlook for German and Japanese rates given the unwelcome pace of the decline in the mark and the strong economic recovery in Japan." Persaud said the prospect of a broad-based start to European economic and monetary union was priced into sterling and was unlikely to provide it with more impetus to go higher. Increasingly vociferous calls from UK businesses to curb sterling's strength have added to the view that some members on the BOE committee might vote to keep rates steady for now after three hikes since May. "The problem for sterling is that the market isn't quite as convinced any more that there will be a rate rise in August, given the negative impact of the strong pound on exporters," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International. Dealers also cited bearish research notes from two major investment houses as weighing on sterling. While German interest rates are expected to remain steady for the foreseeable future, talk surfaced last week that the Bundesbank might switch to a variable repo tender from the fixed rates it has set since August 1996. While the talk proved unfounded after last week's council meeting, traders were intrigued by the Bundesbank's decision to announce fixed rate tenders for the next two weeks even though it went into summer recess for a month. "That should keep speculation about a variable rate bubbling," said a German bank trader. The dollar has surged in the wake of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's upbeat Humphrey-Hawkins testimony last week. A sharp dollar/mark rally has spread into a broad-based dollar rally. Dollar/mark stood at 1.8455/65 at 1620 GMT, up from 1.8354/64 in late European trading on Friday but off its 1.8490 high. The dollar set a four-year peak at 1.5250 Swiss franc before easing back to 1.5173/80 in late Europe, up from 1.5128/38 at the prevous close in Europe. Against the yen, it traded at 117.55/65 from 116.70/80 in late trade here on Friday. Sterling dropped below 3.01 marks and $1.63 in late trade. The pound was at session lows of 3.0078/88, down from an intraday high at 3.0627 and from 3.0560/70 at the European close on Friday. Sterling/dollar stood at $1.6298/08, its lowest level in Europe, and down from a $1.6620 high earlier and from $1.6616/26 in late Europe on Friday. Despite the soft sterling tone, many dealers remain confident that sterling has not reached a top yet. "We remain bullish on sterling. It will be bought back at the lows as dealers continue to bet on higher UK rates," said Stamenkovic at DKB. -- London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
